phases.title: Freeze the research charter
phases.goal: Translate the user vision into falsifiable capture, optics, film, catalogue, and reliability requirements without promising unmeasured hardware modes.
phases.method: Record must-have outcomes, conditional experiments, prohibited claims, and excluded cloud generation. Give every requirement a stable ID, an observable owner, a dependency, and a measurement class. Separate visual preference from numerical correctness and commercial claims.
phases.fixture: A charter containing RAW-derived Log, six virtual formats, offline development, clean-master retention, and an unsupported claim that an SDR filter increases sensor dynamic range.
phases.oracle: The linter accepts the supported categories and rejects the unsupported sensor claim while retaining it in an explicit research-question field.
phases.mutant: Replace a conditional device capability with an unconditional supported flag.
phases.deliverable: Versioned research charter and requirement-to-evidence index

phases.title: Inspect rather than replace the application
phases.goal: Identify reusable production seams before introducing any alternative framework or module hierarchy.
phases.method: Read the live default branch, build configuration, recorder owners, source formats, existing tests, and recovery journal. Record exact blob and commit identities. Map proposed components onto existing packages; add folders only where a concrete ownership boundary warrants them.
phases.fixture: A repository snapshot with existing RAW source readers and on-device development plus an untracked collaborator change.
phases.oracle: The integration plan reuses available interfaces, preserves the collaborator change, and distinguishes inspected files from uninspected code.
phases.mutant: Assume the README is a complete source-code audit and schedule a duplicate camera engine.
phases.deliverable: Repository continuity map and minimal-change architecture decision

phases.title: Build the evidence vocabulary
phases.goal: Prevent theoretical support, sample receipt, successful decoding, and physical qualification from collapsing into one boolean.
phases.method: Define independently recorded stages and evidence references. A stage transition requires its own artefact and validation policy. Bind positive results to the exact mode, device build, lens route, codec, profile, duration, and environment; support explicit unavailable outcomes.
phases.fixture: An advertised 8K candidate with a configured session but no encoded frames, alongside a fully decoded synthetic ten-bit ramp.
phases.oracle: Neither record is eligible for a physical S23 certification badge; the ramp is only codec or arithmetic evidence.
phases.mutant: Calculate device certification as advertised OR decoded instead of requiring relevant independent gates.
phases.deliverable: Evidence schema, classifier, and truthfulness unit tests

phases.title: Establish a reproducible baseline
phases.goal: Create a baseline against which every later claim of improvement can be inspected.
phases.method: Build the unmodified known revision with pinned tools. Execute its existing host and emulator tests without changing thresholds. Preserve logs, commands, dependency identities, failing tests, and skipped hardware probes. Record baseline source hashes separately from generated artefacts.
phases.fixture: A baseline run containing passing host tests, a failing emulator test, and unavailable physical hardware.
phases.oracle: The report preserves all three outcomes and does not convert unavailable into passed or silently repair the baseline before recording it.
phases.mutant: Drop failing test cases from the generated summary.
phases.deliverable: Baseline report, reproducible commands, and captured test outputs

phases.title: Define measurement uncertainty
phases.goal: Make quantitative goals explicit about units, uncertainty, calibration, and statistical scope.
phases.method: Create a metric registry with measurement domain, units, sampling procedure, uncertainty sources, provisional thresholds, and revision history. Distinguish bit depth from effective sensor precision, average cadence from per-frame integrity, and appearance preference from colorimetric error.
phases.fixture: A cadence series with correct average rate but one duplicated frame, plus a noisy chart measurement with an unknown illuminant.
phases.oracle: The cadence integrity test fails despite the mean, and chart results remain exploratory rather than calibrated color certification.
phases.mutant: Report only aggregate means and discard outliers before analysis.
phases.deliverable: Metric registry and uncertainty-budget templates

phases.title: Set decision and risk gates
phases.goal: Make high-risk work conditional on demonstrated benefit rather than fascination with low-level access.
phases.method: Maintain a risk register covering footage loss, misleading labels, thermal load, rendering instability, licensing, and firmware modification. Define reversible experiments first. A gate records alternatives, evidence, resource cost, fallback, and an explicit stop condition.
phases.fixture: A proposed firmware experiment that has no identified blocked stream and no verified recovery procedure.
phases.oracle: The experiment is deferred while non-destructive capability and application-level investigations remain available.
phases.mutant: Treat user enthusiasm for firmware as authorization for an irreversible flash.
phases.deliverable: Risk register and phase-entry decision log

phases.title: Establish a provenance ledger
phases.goal: Make every imported fixture, profile, model, reference frame, and generated result traceable.
phases.method: Create content-addressed provenance records with local identifiers, source attribution, licence review state, permitted use, acquisition date, and transformation history. Keep media access tokens and user identifiers out of public manifests. Unknown rights block redistribution, not private comparison by default.
phases.fixture: Two identically named stock profiles with different hashes and an image whose redistribution permission is unknown.
phases.oracle: The system treats the profiles as distinct versions and excludes the unapproved image from the public bundle.
phases.mutant: Key profile identity only by its display name.
phases.deliverable: Provenance ledger, rights-state validator, and attribution export

phases.title: Publish the execution protocol
phases.goal: Make the master directive executable by another developer without encouraging uncontrolled parallel edits.
phases.method: Define how an agent selects the next dependency-ready phase, writes a failing test, implements the smallest correct change, records evidence, and integrates on the existing branch. Require remote-head verification before an authorized push and a truthful blocked report when access is absent.
phases.fixture: A phase whose host gate passes but physical-device gate is pending, with a concurrent remote commit.
phases.oracle: The phase is reported software-verified only, the remote change is preserved, and completion is not invented.
phases.mutant: Mark every phase complete because the local build succeeded.
phases.deliverable: Agent operating protocol and handoff schema

phases.title: Inventory logical and physical camera routes
phases.goal: Enumerate usable routes without assuming that a physical camera ID is independently openable.
phases.method: Read logical IDs, physical membership, available request keys, focal metadata, and sensor orientation. Preserve nulls and exceptions per property. Build route identities that include the logical owner and requested physical target, then verify result metadata after opening.
phases.fixture: A logical rear camera exposing a physical member not listed as a public camera ID, plus a route with missing focal metadata.
phases.oracle: The planner uses the logical owner for the member and displays unknown focal information without inventing a lens.
phases.mutant: Open every physical member as an independent camera.
phases.deliverable: Camera-route inventory and routing contract tests

phases.title: Enumerate ordinary stream configurations
phases.goal: Preserve every advertised format and size while correctly treating timing data as constraints.
phases.method: Collect output sizes, minimum frame durations, stall durations, and relevant stream combinations. Keep ordinary, high-speed, and maximum-resolution maps separate. Represent missing durations explicitly; do not derive sustained video throughput from a still-image size.
phases.fixture: A RAW size with a long minimum duration and a larger JPEG size available only for still capture.
phases.oracle: The mode list retains both facts but offers neither as proven real-time RAW video.
phases.mutant: Copy the maximum JPEG dimensions into the video capability table.
phases.deliverable: Complete stream map export and timing-aware mode candidates

phases.title: Model rational capture timing
phases.goal: Separate requested output cadence from the sensor timing mechanism that can actually produce it.
phases.method: Represent rates as numerator and denominator. Distinguish fixed AE ranges, variable AE ranges, and manual frame duration. Verify requested exposure does not exceed the effective interval and compare capture-result timing rather than assuming a requested value was applied.
phases.fixture: An AE range of fifteen to thirty frames per second, a requested twenty-four frame output, and manual timing that has not been confirmed.
phases.oracle: The planner cannot label the candidate native fixed twenty-four merely by assigning container timestamps.
phases.mutant: Round an AE upper bound to the nearest desired cinematic frame rate.
phases.deliverable: Rational timing policy and manual-readiness gate

phases.title: Discover dynamic-range profiles
phases.goal: Select HDR-derived paths only when the camera and stream combination support the actual profile.
phases.method: Query ten-bit capability and supported dynamic-range profiles. Evaluate pairwise or set constraints for preview and recording outputs. Record additional latency information where exposed. Keep HLG, HDR10, SDR, and RAW-derived Log as separate source and encoding categories.
phases.fixture: An HLG-capable route that rejects an SDR preview in the same capture request.
phases.oracle: The planner rejects the mixed combination or explicitly chooses an independently qualified monitoring route.
phases.mutant: Assume HLG support implies arbitrary SDR and HDR surface coexistence.
phases.deliverable: Profile-combination planner and explicit rejection reasons

phases.title: Discover codec input routes
phases.goal: Qualify codec interfaces independently rather than treating HEVC Main10 as proof of every ten-bit input route.
phases.method: Inventory codec names, profiles, levels, sizes, rates, surface support, and byte-buffer or Image formats. A P010 developer and an EGL surface encoder have different prerequisites. Store failures per candidate and re-query after relevant device software changes.
phases.fixture: A codec advertising Main10 with surface input but no usable P010 Image input.
phases.oracle: The surface candidate remains available for testing while the CPU P010 developer is honestly unavailable.
phases.mutant: Use the advertised Main10 profile as the sole P010 acceptance criterion.
phases.deliverable: Codec-route database and interface-specific qualification plan

phases.title: Plan native high-resolution experiments
phases.goal: Keep 4K and 8K ambitions visible without promising unmeasured sensor or processing throughput.
phases.method: Construct candidate tuples for advertised sizes, including the user targets where exposed. Require independent capture, encode, decode, cadence, storage, and thermal experiments. Track native geometry separately from crop, binning, downsampling, and upscaling.
phases.fixture: A file declared as 7680 by 4320 whose source was a smaller stream enlarged by the renderer.
phases.oracle: The result is labelled upscaled output and cannot satisfy the native 8K acceptance requirement.
phases.mutant: Validate native resolution using only the container width and height.
phases.deliverable: High-resolution experiment matrix and source-geometry evidence

phases.title: Cache capability evidence safely
phases.goal: Reuse expensive diagnostics without letting obsolete firmware or codec evidence survive a changed environment.
phases.method: Key cached probes by build fingerprint, app protocol version, route, and codec identity. Separate immutable historical measurements from the current selection cache. Revalidate stale candidates on selection and retain a reason when a previously working mode becomes unavailable.
phases.fixture: A firmware update with the same marketing phone name but a changed codec capability response.
phases.oracle: The old report remains inspectable while the current planner refuses to certify the changed route from stale data.
phases.mutant: Key the cache only by the string Galaxy S23 Ultra.
phases.deliverable: Capability cache invalidation and historical evidence viewer

phases.title: Run the first physical qualification slice
phases.goal: Establish a modest complete device path before escalating resolution or adding expensive effects.
phases.method: Choose one actually available rear route and conservative advertised configuration. Capture a controlled sixty-second take with a visible timing event and audio when supported. Decode it fully, inspect source and output metadata, and preserve thermal and storage observations.
phases.fixture: A real phone take with a single missing sample near thermal escalation and an otherwise playable output.
phases.oracle: The file is retained, playback integrity and cadence receive separate statuses, and the mode is not endurance-certified.
phases.mutant: Accept a mode after checking only the first decoded frame.
phases.deliverable: Physical qualification report for one exact configuration

phases.title: Model camera resource ownership
phases.goal: Guarantee one owner and one terminal release for each camera device, session, surface, and Image.
phases.method: Draw the ownership graph and implement closeable leases with generation identity. Separate application-owned capture work from Activity attachment. Propagate failure through typed events and close resources in a defined reverse dependency order.
phases.fixture: A session callback arriving after its Activity has been recreated and its previous surface released.
phases.oracle: The callback cannot attach to the new generation or double-close a resource; the active preview remains valid.
phases.mutant: Reuse a surface solely because its previous object reference is non-null.
phases.deliverable: Resource-lifetime map and deterministic owner tests

phases.title: Implement the capture state reducer
phases.goal: Make recording readiness and termination explicit, replayable, and resistant to late callbacks.
phases.method: Use distinct opening, preview, configuring, starting, recording, stopping, finalizing, and failure states. Every asynchronous event carries a generation token. First-sample acknowledgement is required before the recording timer and active indicator change.
phases.fixture: Record followed immediately by Stop, with a delayed first video sample and a delayed audio format callback.
phases.oracle: The state never returns from stopping to recording and the retained output receives an accurate terminal status.
phases.mutant: Allow any first-frame callback to set recording=true.
phases.deliverable: Pure reducer, event log format, and race replay tests

phases.title: Implement applied manual exposure
phases.goal: Require result-confirmed manual exposure rather than trusting requested ISO and shutter fields.
phases.method: Validate units and sensor limits, clamp only through a visible effective target, wait for the required lock transition, and compare actual result values against defined tolerances. Preserve the difference between missing metadata and a measured mismatch.
phases.fixture: A requested shutter longer than the frame period and an ISO result that remains at the previous automatic value.
phases.oracle: The user sees the effective target and mismatch; recording cannot claim confirmed manual control.
phases.mutant: Show requested ISO as if it were an observed sensor value.
phases.deliverable: Manual exposure controller and result-matching tests

phases.title: Implement stable white-balance controls
phases.goal: Separate hardware white balance, scene calibration, and creative temperature adjustments.
phases.method: Expose available presets and locks, record gains and transforms where accessible, and label Kelvin values provisional unless independently calibrated. A creative tint slider changes the render recipe, not capture metadata. Avoid changing the RAW neutral interpretation without versioning the profile.
phases.fixture: A stable RAW neutral point with a creative warm preview and an unsupported hardware Kelvin request.
phases.oracle: The source metadata stays unchanged, the preview recipe records its adjustment, and unsupported Kelvin remains unavailable.
phases.mutant: Write a creative temperature slider value into measured sensor white-balance evidence.
phases.deliverable: White-balance intent model and capture-versus-look separation

phases.title: Implement focus intent and observed lens state
phases.goal: Distinguish physical lens focus from the virtual focus plane used during development.
phases.method: Keep separate control namespaces and units. Confirm physical focus through available results and expose unknown distance honestly. Virtual focus may track a subject in relative depth without claiming metric distance; recording source sharpness remains independently important.
phases.fixture: A face selected for virtual focus while the physical lens is focused on a nearby foreground object.
phases.oracle: The interface warns that virtual refocusing cannot restore source detail that was never sharply recorded.
phases.mutant: Overwrite the physical focus-distance field with the virtual focus target.
phases.deliverable: Dual focus model and focus provenance tests

phases.title: Protect preview independence
phases.goal: Ensure framing aids, display transforms, and UI rendering cannot contaminate the clean master.
phases.method: Branch monitoring after the declared source normalization point. Give the preview its own downsample, display transform, overlays, and freshness metadata. Tests must compare the recorded pixels or source hashes with preview aids enabled and disabled.
phases.fixture: A false-color overlay, histogram update, and virtual-film preview changed repeatedly during the same synthetic capture sequence.
phases.oracle: The clean master remains identical within its deterministic capture contract and overlays appear only in monitoring.
phases.mutant: Reuse the composited preview framebuffer as the supposedly untouched recording source.
phases.deliverable: Monitoring branch contract and clean-master invariance test

phases.title: Handle interruption and permission changes
phases.goal: Preserve footage and communicate state when the application loses access to camera or microphone.
phases.method: Define responses to permission denial, camera preemption, screen departure, app backgrounding, and device policy restrictions. Follow the existing visible stop-and-finalize policy unless a separately qualified background design is approved. Never silently remove a requested audio track.
phases.fixture: Microphone permission revoked during startup while video samples are already arriving.
phases.oracle: The take stops or fails visibly under policy, retains available media, and cannot be labelled a successful audio recording.
phases.mutant: Continue silently as video-only after requested microphone acquisition fails.
phases.deliverable: Interruption policy and permission fault tests

phases.title: Bound capture queues and backpressure
phases.goal: Keep slow consumers from causing unbounded memory use or silently losing sensor frames.
phases.method: Budget queues in bytes and frames, use explicit policies for preview drops versus source failure, and instrument outstanding leases. Source overflow causes a controlled visible stop with gap evidence. Preview and ML queues may discard stale work without altering source timestamps.
phases.fixture: A depth worker blocked for several seconds while the source writer remains healthy, followed by a deliberately stalled source writer.
phases.oracle: The first condition only reduces monitoring freshness; the second triggers a documented capture stop rather than hidden loss.
phases.mutant: Use one unbounded queue for source writing, preview, and inference.
phases.deliverable: Backpressure policies and bounded-memory stress harness

phases.title: Specify clock domains and epochs
phases.goal: Create an explicit mapping between sensor, monotonic system, codec, and audio clocks.
phases.method: Represent every timestamp with domain and units. Estimate clock correspondence only using an identified method and retained samples. Use a shared take epoch for presentation while preserving original sensor times. Mark unsupported synchronization paths as unverified.
phases.fixture: Audio and video streams whose timestamps look similar numerically but originate from different clock domains.
phases.oracle: The synchronizer refuses to assume equivalence without a measured or documented mapping.
phases.mutant: Subtract timestamps from unrelated domains because both are expressed in nanoseconds.
phases.deliverable: Clock-domain types and timing evidence schema

phases.title: Qualify video encoder startup
phases.goal: Start a take only when the selected codec route produces usable samples with the expected signal contract.
phases.method: Handle format changes, codec-config buffers, keyframe requests, and startup timeouts separately. Inspect the actual output profile and bit depth. Retain diagnostic reasons for an advertised codec that fails configuration or produces the wrong signal.
phases.fixture: A Main10 request that yields an eight-bit SPS after a successful configure call.
phases.oracle: The output fails the ten-bit route gate and is not silently relabelled as acceptable Log.
phases.mutant: Validate codec depth from the requested MediaFormat rather than the emitted stream.
phases.deliverable: Encoder startup owner and output-signal checks

phases.title: Qualify microphone acquisition
phases.goal: Make audio an independently owned acquisition path with explicit channel and permission semantics.
phases.method: Use bounded PCM transfer, report actual format and route, preserve clipping and silencing evidence, and separate acquisition from AAC callbacks. Microphone route changes are events with an explicit continue or stop policy, never invisible configuration drift.
phases.fixture: A stereo request routed to a mono source and a deliberate encoder stall while microphone acquisition continues.
phases.oracle: The output describes actual channels, queue limits hold, and acquisition timing distinguishes encoder delay from missing microphone data.
phases.mutant: Report requested stereo when only one source channel exists.
phases.deliverable: Audio acquisition contract and blocked-encoder tests

phases.title: Implement two-track startup and drain
phases.goal: Prevent playable-looking video files that silently omit requested audio or truncate one track.
phases.method: Wait for all selected track formats before starting the muxer. Bound pre-start samples, coordinate EOS independently, and define maximum drain duration. Record which track failed and preserve useful partial output under an unverified label.
phases.fixture: Video format arrives immediately, audio format arrives late, then Stop occurs before audio EOS.
phases.oracle: The state machine produces the correct incomplete or verified outcome without deadlock or fabricated audio samples.
phases.mutant: Start the muxer after the first track and ignore later selected tracks.
phases.deliverable: Two-track mux protocol and EOS fault tests

phases.title: Preserve cadence rather than hide gaps
phases.goal: Detect timing defects before any optional conversion to constant-frame-rate output.
phases.method: Analyze original timestamp intervals, duplicates, discontinuities, duration, and count. Keep packet ordering distinct from presentation ordering when codec reordering exists. Any retiming is a named development operation with mapping metadata, not repair disguised as native capture.
phases.fixture: A source containing one forty-eight-millisecond gap and a later short interval that restores the average frame rate.
phases.oracle: The per-frame integrity gate reports the gap even when the final average falls within tolerance.
phases.mutant: Approve cadence using only total frames divided by duration.
phases.deliverable: Cadence analyzer and source-to-output time mapping

phases.title: Publish media transactionally
phases.goal: Make verified publication a separate transaction from capture and auxiliary report writing.
phases.method: Write into private staging, inspect output, copy or move according to the actual storage provider semantics, commit publication, and only then remove redundant staging. Budget temporary duplication. Failed report export must leave media intact and discoverable.
phases.fixture: A full gallery destination after private recording succeeds, followed by a report serialization exception.
phases.oracle: The source remains in recovery storage, no empty gallery success is shown, and the error identifies the failed publication step.
phases.mutant: Delete private staging before the public copy is durably accepted.
phases.deliverable: Publication state machine and storage-pressure tests

phases.title: Recover interrupted recordings
phases.goal: Make restart recovery evidence-driven, conservative, and non-destructive.
phases.method: Journal path identity, take metadata, selected tracks, and terminal status. On cold start, inspect nonempty remnants without assuming an unfinished MP4 is playable. Offer explicit export and retry, and require confirmation before deleting the sole retained copy.
phases.fixture: Process termination during muxer finalization with both a nonempty partial file and an incomplete journal record.
phases.oracle: The recovery library exposes the artefact as unverified and does not discard it merely because normal validation cannot complete.
phases.mutant: Delete every file lacking a completed journal flag.
phases.deliverable: Cold-start recovery scanner and interrupted-file fixtures

phases.title: Measure physical audiovisual synchronization
phases.goal: Validate capture with a real event, not only aligned packet timestamps.
phases.method: Record repeatable visible and audible events under documented geometry, estimate offsets independently, and report measurement uncertainty. Use multiple events across a longer take to separate fixed offset from drift. Account for sound travel when the fixture distance matters.
phases.fixture: A flash-and-click recording with a constant offset at the beginning and increased offset near the end.
phases.oracle: The report distinguishes initial synchronization error from drift and does not certify lip sync from container starts alone.
phases.mutant: Use matching first packet timestamps as the sole synchronization test.
phases.deliverable: Physical audiovisual protocol and measured offset report

phases.title: Specify the RAW sequence container
phases.goal: Define a bounded, versioned recording format before optimizing its writer.
phases.method: Include file magic, schema version, route identity, source geometry, CFA, packing, calibration snapshot, and per-frame metadata. Frame records need lengths, timestamps, integrity checks, and explicit end state. Readers must reject impossible lengths before allocation.
phases.fixture: A valid three-frame source followed by an oversized length field and a truncated final record.
phases.oracle: The reader reports the complete prefix and corruption separately under an explicit recovery mode without rewriting the original.
phases.mutant: Allocate an arbitrary declared payload length before checking bounds.
phases.deliverable: RAW source specification and hostile-input reader tests

phases.title: Pair Images with exact capture metadata
phases.goal: Prevent exposure, black-level, or neutral metadata from drifting onto the wrong sensor frame.
phases.method: Join by exact sensor timestamp using bounded pending maps. Define timeout and missing-metadata policy. Detect duplicate timestamps and preserve partial results rather than nearest-neighbor guessing. Close every Image after copying or consuming its data.
phases.fixture: Frames arriving out of callback order with one metadata entry delayed and another absent.
phases.oracle: Only exact matches enter qualified source records; unresolved frames receive an explicit failure or gap policy.
phases.mutant: Attach the most recently received metadata to each incoming Image.
phases.deliverable: Exact pairing service and reorder-timeout tests

phases.title: Implement packed RAW decoding fixtures
phases.goal: Make packing and row-stride errors visible before any demosaic or color transform.
phases.method: Construct tiny synthetic mosaics for supported RAW formats with known code values, row padding, crop offsets, and all CFA parities. Use independent bit-level references. Do not assume RAW_SENSOR, RAW10, and RAW12 have interchangeable memory layouts.
phases.fixture: Alternating minimum and maximum sample codes in padded rows with a crop beginning on an odd coordinate.
phases.oracle: Decoded codes and CFA coordinates match the independent fixture exactly, with padding untouched.
phases.mutant: Read every source as contiguous sixteen-bit native-endian samples.
phases.deliverable: Packing adapters and exact golden arrays

phases.title: Build the acquisition-only throughput probe
phases.goal: Measure sensor delivery independently of expensive disk writes and development.
phases.method: Use preallocated buffers and counters to measure intervals, occupancy, copy time, and sustained delivery for a bounded run. State clearly when frames are not retained. Keep acquisition-only results separate from saved-source throughput and final encoded performance.
phases.fixture: A route delivering frames regularly when discarded but losing cadence when written to storage.
phases.oracle: The report preserves the distinction and cannot claim the faster acquisition-only rate as reliable recorded RAW video.
phases.mutant: Publish the best acquisition-only rate as the recording capability.
phases.deliverable: Acquisition probe and stage-separated throughput report

phases.title: Build the bounded saved-source writer
phases.goal: Write continuous RAW records without blocking camera callbacks indefinitely.
phases.method: Transfer owned copies through a fixed-capacity pool to an independent writer. Record short writes, flush policy, source count, and overflow. A full pool stops acquisition explicitly; it must not silently overwrite an older frame or invent replacement timestamps.
phases.fixture: A source writer paused until the copy pool fills, then resumed after the capture controller has stopped.
phases.oracle: All retained records remain ordered and intact, overflow is visible, and late completion cannot resume the failed take.
phases.mutant: Overwrite the oldest queued source frame to keep a green recording indicator.
phases.deliverable: Bounded RAW writer and deterministic overflow harness

phases.title: Snapshot calibration metadata at capture time
phases.goal: Retain enough source context for later development without pretending metadata is a measured profile.
phases.method: Capture available calibration and forward matrices, reference illuminants, neutral points, black and white levels, crop descriptions, and lens shading data with explicit missing fields. Bind snapshots to firmware and route. Document the coordinate and matrix conventions.
phases.fixture: Two takes on different firmware versions with different forward matrices but the same physical handset.
phases.oracle: The developer selects the matching snapshot and rejects a profile whose source identity does not match.
phases.mutant: Look up current camera metadata while developing an older source and treat it as capture-time truth.
phases.deliverable: Capture-time calibration snapshot and identity checks

phases.title: Retain sources across cancelled development
phases.goal: Guarantee that failed or cancelled exports cannot mutate or delete the original RAW sequence.
phases.method: Use read-only source handles, separate destination identities, and content hashes before and after processing. Manage temporary output independently. Cancellation closes leases and records progress while preserving source and profile records.
phases.fixture: Cancellation halfway through development followed by a process restart and a retry with another film recipe.
phases.oracle: The source hash is unchanged, the partial result is labelled incomplete, and the retry reads the original frames.
phases.mutant: Reuse the source filename as the destination of a developed movie.
phases.deliverable: Non-destructive development contract and cancellation tests

phases.title: Qualify saved RAW on the physical S23
phases.goal: Establish what sustained RAW capture actually works on the particular phone.
phases.method: Run successively longer conservative experiments only after acquisition and writer gates pass. Measure sample integrity, source completeness, metadata availability, storage bandwidth, thermal state, and lens behaviour. Keep maximum-resolution experiments conditional on lower-cost results.
phases.fixture: A five-second successful RAW sequence followed by a sixty-second run that stops under severe thermal pressure.
phases.oracle: The app reports the measured duration boundaries and retains the longer partial take rather than extrapolating endurance.
phases.mutant: Treat a five-frame still sequence as proof of sustained RAW video.
phases.deliverable: Physical RAW qualification matrix and retained source fixtures

phases.title: Define the calibrated profile contract
phases.goal: Make a profile an accountable measurement record rather than a collection of unnamed matrices.
phases.method: Specify source identity, matrix direction, white point, exposure scale, crop, CFA assumptions, illuminant, black model, defect policy, and fit provenance. Separate measured, manufacturer-derived provisional, and synthetic profiles. Hash the complete numerical payload and reject nonfinite values.
phases.fixture: A profile labelled measured but lacking measurement references, plus a synthetic profile offered for physical footage.
phases.oracle: The importer retains the author assertion separately and refuses synthetic evidence as physical calibration.
phases.mutant: Promote any imported profile with a measured string to certified status.
phases.deliverable: Profile schema and provenance-aware importer

phases.title: Measure black response and read noise
phases.goal: Characterize dark behaviour without crushing signed noise or interpreting denoising as sensor improvement.
phases.method: Acquire controlled dark sequences at selected exposure and gain settings. Inspect row, column, temporal, and hot-pixel structure. Preserve signed residuals after black subtraction, report uncertainty, and separate sensor code saturation from later normalization.
phases.fixture: Dark frames containing a small negative mean after an intentionally incorrect black subtraction and a persistent hot column.
phases.oracle: The fit detects the bias and structured defect rather than clipping all negative samples to zero.
phases.mutant: Clamp black-subtracted RAW to zero before computing statistics.
phases.deliverable: Black-level model and dark-frame analysis report

phases.title: Measure flat-field and lens shading
phases.goal: Correct spatial gain only when the illumination and coordinate conventions are controlled.
phases.method: Capture diffuse uniform fields, reject gradients caused by the light source, align calibration to the actual crop and CFA, and bound correction gains. Record lens, focus, aperture metadata where applicable, exposure, and firmware. Validate on a separate flat capture.
phases.fixture: A flat field with a deliberate illumination gradient and a mismatched crop origin.
phases.oracle: The pipeline does not absorb the lighting gradient into a supposedly universal lens-shading correction and detects coordinate mismatch.
phases.mutant: Apply a shading map in display coordinates after rotation.
phases.deliverable: Flat-field acquisition protocol and shading-map validator

phases.title: Establish neutral exposure scale
phases.goal: Use a known neutral target to establish exposure normalization without overstating what it measures.
phases.method: Inspect a user-confirmed patch for clipping, texture, signal level, and color neutrality. Retain ROI coordinates and source frame identity. Apply exposure scale separately from chromatic fitting, and reject invalid patches rather than silently guessing from the whole frame.
phases.fixture: A bright white object misidentified as eighteen-percent grey and a grey patch partly clipped by a specular reflection.
phases.oracle: The calibration workflow requests valid evidence and records uncertainty instead of producing a confidently measured scale.
phases.mutant: Assume the mean image luminance always corresponds to middle grey.
phases.deliverable: Neutral-reference measurement and guarded scale estimator

phases.title: Fit color transforms with held-out validation
phases.goal: Estimate a useful camera-to-working transform without overfitting a single chart photograph.

phases.title: Define the movie evidence schema

phases.title: Version creative reconstruction parameters

phases.fixture: A user changes the virtual aperture and print contrast of a movie-inspired recipe.

phases.title: Implement offline search and filtering
phases.goal: Make the catalogue useful without network dependence or opaque recommendation behavior.
phases.method: Index titles, alternate titles, stock names, formats, scene families, and evidence quality. Support typo-tolerant discovery with explicit matching behavior. Keep local user recipes private and allow sorting by relevant technical criteria rather than invented popularity.

phases.oracle: The correct local candidates appear with their evidence status and no network request is required.

phases.deliverable: Offline search index and deterministic retrieval tests

phases.title: Manage reference media rights and attribution
phases.goal: Avoid bundling copyrighted frames or proprietary look data without the required permission.
phases.method: Store links and factual citations separately from distributable assets. Use owned comparison footage and approved thumbnails. Track model, profile, LUT, image, and text rights independently. Unknown redistribution status blocks packaging that asset until reviewed.
phases.fixture: A useful production still with an accessible public URL but no permission to bundle it in the app.
phases.oracle: The catalogue can retain a citation while excluding the image bytes from the distributable package.

phases.title: Implement constrained reference matching
phases.goal: Use optional analysis to suggest renderer parameters without replacing source content.
phases.method: Analyze approved reference material for broad color, tone, texture, and contrast characteristics. Fit bounded parameters in our renderer, preserve scene structure, and expose the result as a suggestion. Keep lighting and composition mismatch visible as limitations.

phases.title: Validate recipe fidelity and honesty
phases.goal: Evaluate whether recipes are coherent and enjoyable without overstating historical or physical accuracy.
phases.method: Use matched owned sources, blind preference tests, parameter ablations, and expert review where possible. Score evidence completeness separately from appearance preference. A popular recipe may remain reconstructed; a well-sourced recipe may need artistic refinement.

phases.deliverable: Recipe evaluation report and catalogue quality policy

phases.title: Build the layered automated test system
phases.goal: Separate host arithmetic, JVM policies, Android integration, GPU parity, and physical acceptance.
phases.method: Run fast deterministic contracts on every change, then focused integration suites and scheduled device experiments. phases.title: Secure media and profile import boundaries

phases.oracle: All inputs fail safely without excessive allocation, file escape, or source corruption.

phases.deliverable: Import threat model and parser fuzz corpus

phases.title: Verify offline privacy and permissions

phases.deliverable: Privacy test report and permission inventory

phases.title: Establish thermal and endurance acceptance
phases.goal: Use conservative safety policies and measured operating envelopes.
phases.method: Run controlled sustained tests across relevant source and render configurations, record ambient conditions and device state, and observe thermal callbacks. phases.deliverable: Endurance protocol and configuration-specific operating envelope

phases.goal: Separate debug convenience from a maintainable release and update process.

phases.goal: Tie every public capability claim to current evidence and documented limits.

phases.method: Review footage retention, crash recovery, color signalling, temporal artifacts, licensing, privacy, accessibility, and update safety. Resolve or explicitly defer noncritical issues. A critical data-loss or misleading-capture defect blocks release regardless of visual quality.

phases.goal: Research the device architecture without modifying the user’s phone.

phases.goal: Exhaust useful normal-app approaches before escalating risk.

phases.goal: Make any authorized low-level change minimal, observable, and reversible where technically possible.

cases.expected: Report the missing capability while preserving ordinary capture and source retention.
cases.negative: An offline camera must not hang waiting for an undisclosed cloud dependency.
cases.repeat: Repeat first installation, asset update, and a previously working offline session.

cases.name: Delegate failure and fallback
cases.intervention: Fail runtime or delegate initialization while a preview or development job is active.
cases.expected: Use only an explicitly qualified fallback or disable optional depth processing with a clear reason.
cases.negative: Silently changing to an untested backend or uploading frames must fail.
cases.repeat: Repeat CPU, GPU, and available accelerator configurations as applicable.

cases.name: Stale depth result
cases.intervention: Delay inference until its result no longer matches the current source timestamp or crop.
cases.expected: Reject or explicitly reproject the result under a validated policy rather than applying it blindly.
cases.negative: A float array without temporal and geometric identity must not be accepted.
cases.repeat: Repeat rapid camera movement, rotation, source switches, and scene cuts.

cases.name: Confidence misrepresentation
cases.intervention: Provide unstable or unreliable predictions while their confidence metadata claims certainty.
cases.expected: Expose uncalibrated confidence and reduce rendering reliance according to the declared policy.
cases.negative: An arbitrary confidence score must not be presented as a calibrated probability.
cases.repeat: Repeat transparent surfaces, low texture, mirrors, and unfamiliar scenes.

cases.name: Integrated load and thermal drift
cases.intervention: Run inference alongside actual capture, rendering, and encoding for a sustained interval.
cases.expected: Measure complete workload behavior and choose live or deferred operation from evidence.
cases.negative: Standalone model latency must not become a full-camera frame-rate guarantee.
cases.repeat: Repeat cold start, warm operation, memory pressure, and severe thermal conditions.

cases.name: Model identity substitution
cases.intervention: Replace a model asset with another variant or converted file while retaining a cached result.
cases.expected: Invalidate incompatible caches and report the actual model identity before accepting depth output.
cases.negative: A filename match alone must not establish identical weights.
cases.repeat: Repeat with precision changes, runtime versions, and different model variants.

cases.name: Preprocessing geometry error
cases.intervention: Use a non-square source with known corner markers and alter resizing, padding, or channel order.
cases.expected: Match the specified tensor preparation and restore output coordinates correctly.
cases.negative: Unrecorded stretching or swapped color channels must fail.
cases.repeat: Repeat portrait, landscape, cropped, and rotated source frames.

cases.name: Conversion accuracy regression
cases.intervention: Compare exported or quantized model results against the approved host baseline on withheld scenes.
cases.expected: Meet declared depth and boundary tolerances or remain experimental despite successful loading.
cases.negative: A model that merely runs is not numerically qualified.
cases.repeat: Repeat hair, glass, low light, thin objects, and saturated illumination.

cases.expected: Use current evidence and uncertainty rather than smearing previous foreground values into the new region.

cases.name: Relative-scale pumping

cases.expected: Align valid relative depth consistently or reset honestly without arbitrary global focus shifts.

cases.repeat: Repeat stationary backgrounds with changing foreground occupancy.

cases.name: Scene-cut contamination

cases.expected: Reset relevant history and prevent previous-image depth or color from leaking into the new shot.
cases.negative: Continuous timestamps alone must not preserve temporal state across a real cut.
cases.repeat: Repeat hard cuts, fades, flashes, and rapid camera pans to test discrimination.

cases.name: Mixed-pixel boundaries

cases.expected: Preserve plausible partial coverage and bound temporal halos under the selected safe settings.
cases.negative: A dilated binary person mask must not pass demanding boundary quality by itself.
cases.repeat: Repeat backlighting, crossing subjects, and different foreground-background contrast.

cases.name: Subject identity crossing
cases.intervention: Let two similar subjects cross while one remains the user-selected focus target.
cases.expected: Follow the documented identity and target-loss policy without unexplained focus jumps.
cases.negative: Choosing the nearest face independently in every frame must fail.
cases.repeat: Repeat brief occlusion, leaving frame, re-entry, and low-confidence tracking.

cases.expected: Respect layering and normalized energy while declaring unavoidable missing-background approximations.
cases.negative: Uniform background blur with no foreground coverage model must fail.
cases.repeat: Repeat perfect-depth and estimated-depth inputs to isolate the faulty subsystem.

cases.name: Rolling-shutter model violation

cases.repeat: Repeat pans, vibrations, moving subjects, and unknown readout timing.

cases.name: Guidance overrides user intent

cases.name: Combined temporal effects

cases.repeat: Repeat one changed identity field at a time and inspect specific rejection reasons.

cases.name: Cancellation at acceptance boundary
cases.intervention: Cancel during rendering, verification, publication, or final cleanup.
cases.expected: Acknowledge cancellation only after ownership is controlled and never publish a cancelled job as accepted.
cases.negative: A late worker callback that reverses cancellation must fail.
cases.repeat: Repeat with process restart and an already retained partial output.

cases.name: Temporary storage exhaustion
cases.intervention: Make remaining space insufficient for intermediate work or duplicate publication storage.
cases.expected: Pause or fail safely before source loss, preserving recoverable artifacts and clear cleanup choices.
cases.negative: Budgeting only final output bytes must fail.
cases.repeat: Repeat before rendering, during chunk assembly, and during gallery publication.

cases.name: Missing or revoked media access
cases.intervention: Revoke the source grant or remove a file while the library still has a cached thumbnail.
cases.expected: Show actual availability and preserve historical metadata without treating the thumbnail as accessible media.
cases.negative: Thumbnail presence must not certify a valid source or output.
cases.repeat: Repeat local files, document-provider grants, and recovered private media.

cases.repeat: Repeat fractional rates, audio-bearing clips, and scene cuts at boundaries.
